ledger_after.text: Use spatial landmarks and explicit grasp-target pairings (e.g., "left edge", "left half", "left-hand corner") instead of abstract directionals to guide manipulation.
Specify the exact destination container material or property (e.g., "metal pot", "drawer", "pot") rather than using generic locative nouns (e.g., "sink area", "sink basin").

Avoid using complex, high-friction state-change verbs (e.g., "Crease", "Straighten out", "Smooth out", "Unroll", "Spread") in favor of direct physical action verbs (e.g., "Fold", "Take", "Bring", "Grab").
Replace generic spatial prepositions (e.g., "in") with highly specific, physically-constrained insertion verbs (e.g., "toss", "transfer", "insert") to improve object-receptacle alignment.
Keep the instruction focused strictly on the target object's primary identity rather than describing its current state or contents (e.g., avoid "pot containing the play food" or "crumpled cloth").
